name: Acute Exacerbation of COPD
description: An acute, sustained worsening of respiratory symptoms beyond the patient's usual stable COPD state. Common manifestations include increased breathlessness, cough, sputum volume and/or sputum purulence. Exacerbations may be triggered by infections, smoking-related exposure, air pollution or other causes and are not always bacterial.
common_symptoms: Change in sputum colour or purulence
associated_symptoms: Fever or systemic symptoms when infection is present
risk_factors: Previous COPD exacerbations or hospital admissions
Air pollution or respiratory irritant exposure
recommended_investigations: Chest X-ray when severe disease or an alternative diagnosis is suspected
Arterial blood gas testing in severe exacerbation or suspected respiratory failure
Sputum culture when clinically indicated, particularly with purulent sputum or poor response
ECG when cardiac disease or another cardiopulmonary cause is suspected
red_flags: Signs of respiratory failure or sepsis
contraindications: Do not assume every COPD exacerbation is bacterial; antibiotic decisions require clinical assessment.
Avoid uncontrolled oxygen administration in patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure; oxygen should be clinically titrated.
